coaching.headline: A 38-minute loss: Legion alone killed four of our five players 16 times combined, including all seven of Muriel's deaths, and we were out-killed 31 to 21 overall despite leading the objective count 25 to 19.
coaching.team: The draft read three lanes unfavored to two favored. The carry lane, Murdock against Legion, and the midlane, Gideon against Neon, both came back "ours all game," while the offlane, Akeron against Shinbi, and the support, Muriel against Steel, read "theirs all game," and the jungle, Khaimera against Aurora, read "theirs early, even late." Akeron took first blood off Shinbi at 2.5, but he was then caught alone by Shinbi at 12.7 and by Aurora at 15.5, a sign of the pressure behind that "theirs early" jungle read. The first big trade came at 9.5: Gideon and Murdock lost a two-on-two at their Fangtooth 0-2, the enemy took that Fangtooth at 10, and we answered by taking the Mini Prime ourselves the next minute. We won the fight at 23.2 three-to-one and cashed it into our own Fangtooth by 24, but gave two fights straight back to Legion and Steel at our own structures shortly after, losing 0-2 twice within about four minutes. The costliest moment came at 30.9: with a 5-versus-3 man advantage, Khaimera, Muriel and Murdock still lost 0-3 to Legion alone, arriving thirty seconds after the enemy had traded a fight elsewhere for the Primal Fangtooth. We answered with a fight at our inhibitor that we won 3-1 and cashed into the Orb Prime, but Murdock was then caught alone by Shinbi, and the four-versus-five fight that followed was lost 1-3, ending the game shortly after. Only one of us carried an anti-heal item against Steel's healing, and only two of five itemized armor against Legion's mostly-physical damage, the same carry who produced those 16 kills across four of our five players. Building around the enemy's fed carry earlier is the one thing to fix next game.
coaching.whatShiftedIt: The stretch that decided the game ran from 24.6 to 30.9. Muriel and Murdock lost back-to-back two-on-two fights to Legion and Steel at our own structures, giving up ground twice in about four minutes without ever being outnumbered. Then at 30.9, arriving fresh off trading a fight for the Primal Fangtooth thirty seconds earlier, Legion alone caught Khaimera, Muriel and Murdock with a 5-versus-3 advantage still in our favor and won it 0-3. Three losses in six minutes, two of them with no numbers disadvantage, let one already-fed hero take over the rest of the game.
coaching.whatWorked: The one clean habit was converting won fights immediately. All three fights won this game were cashed into a tower or objective within 90 seconds each, a perfect conversion rate against the enemy's 6 cashes on 7 wins. The clearest example was the fight at 23.2, three-to-one, which turned into the Fangtooth by 24.

perPlayer.10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim's Gideon won the midlane read "ours all game" against Neon and built the exact winning core, Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings, with zero off-meta slots, adding Oblivion Crown on top. That gave him the team's second-highest hero damage, 36,553, behind only Akeron. But he died seven times, three of them to Steel and two to Neon, and the macro data flags him as alive and ahead in his own lane, yet absent, from four of the team's fights, including the 0-3 loss at 30.9 with a man advantage still in hand. A lane that far ahead needs to close in and change those numbers, not keep farming it out.
perPlayer.a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs's Khaimera faced a jungle matchup against Aurora that read "theirs early, even late," and Aurora caught him alone once, at 14.4. He finished with the team's highest damage taken, 72,251, and highest damage to objectives, 32,378, going 5 kills and 5 deaths. His build hit two of the three winning-core items, Overlord and Basilisk, skipping only Rapture for Void Helm and two off-meta pieces; Rapture's on-hit damage and lifesteal are dueling tools that might have helped in the extended trades with Aurora and Legion that ran up that damage total.
perPlayer.fed26803-69a9-4fa1-b140-21f3cdf8d8e3: Matthewbernotas9's Akeron had the best individual read on our side of the box score, 4 kills, 3 deaths, 7 assists, and the team's highest mitigated damage, 68,896, plus 18,188 healing done from his own kit. He killed Shinbi three times, including the game's first blood at 2.5, yet the lane still read "theirs all game" the whole game. His build skipped all three winning-core items, Magnify, Tainted Scepter and Truesilver Bracelet, going instead for Cybernetic Drive, Megacosm, Fire Blossom, Flux Matrix and Plasma Blade, a heavily defensive off-meta path that included none of Tainted Scepter's healing cut against Steel. That left the team's most durable player without the anti-heal answer, on a night the team carried only one anti-heal item total.
perPlayer.ed187ebf-450b-4f23-be5e-cb691e6328fe: Bman2295 won the carry lane read "ours all game" against Legion and built the hero's exact winning core, Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator, adding Tainted Rounds, the team's only anti-heal item on the night. It didn't show up in the score: 6 kills, 9 deaths, 1 assist, the team's lowest kda. Legion killed him four times and Steel twice, and seven of his nine deaths were followed by a lost tower or objective within 90 seconds, more than any other player. The lane win never turned into map pressure once the fighting moved past laning.
perPlayer.ae57df87-d868-498b-af8b-4562f987f67a: Muriel had the toughest individual matchup of the night, the support lane read "theirs all game" against Steel, and Legion killed her in all seven of her deaths. She placed the team's most wards, 26, but her own healing, 11,031, came in lower than both Akeron's and Khaimera's, despite being the team's only listed healer. The build skipped all three winning-core items, Marshal, Crystal Tear and Windcaller; two of those, Crystal Tear and Windcaller, boost outgoing healing and shielding by 12%, and none of it was built, running Golem's Gift, Spellbreaker and Gaussian Greaves instead. Against the enemy carry who ended her every death, more of that amplification behind the shields might have mattered.

30.9.call: With a 5-versus-3 man advantage still in hand, Khaimera, Muriel and Murdock lost this fight 0-3 to Legion alone, thirty seconds after the enemy had traded a fight elsewhere for the Primal Fangtooth. Being up two bodies and still losing the fight is the moment that should have forced a full regroup instead of pressing three into an already-fed Legion.

37.5.call: Murdock had been caught alone by Shinbi about 45 seconds earlier, so this fight opened four-versus-five before a hit landed, and it went to Legion and Shinbi 1-3. Waiting for the fifth member back, rather than taking a fight already down a body against the game's best-performing player, was the better call with the game on the line.

33.8.call: With Murdock dead but Legion also out of the fight, the team fought this one even, 4-versus-4, and still won it 3-1, cashing it straight into the Orb Prime. Winning an even fight down our own carry, then converting it into an objective immediately, is exactly the shape of fight worth repeating.

10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.build: Willy Guggenheim's Gideon completed the hero's exact winning core, Azure Core, Combustion and Wraith Leggings, then added Oblivion Crown, with zero off-meta slots on the night. Azure Core's on-cast shield and stacking mana keep a mage alive through poke, Combustion detonates area damage around whatever it hits, and Wraith Leggings adds 12% bonus magic damage to every ability, a burst-scaling trio that Oblivion Crown's flat 25% magic power then multiplies further. That fully-built path is a real part of why 36,553 hero damage came in as the team's second-highest, behind only Akeron, even in a losing game. The build never itemized any defense, which matched a hero whose win condition is landing burst from range rather than surviving a dive.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a.eternal: Vesh fits an area-burst mage like Gideon: every ability hit that lands on a hero adds a damage-over-time tick worth 6% of that hit, plus 0.5% more per minute, rewarding a kit whose Cosmic Rift and Black Hole both hit multiple targets at once. It adds no health or armor of its own, so the loadout is a bet on landing the combo rather than trading blows directly, which fits a midlane matchup that read "ours all game" against Neon rather than a dive-heavy one.

a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.build: Xeebs hit two of the three winning-core items, Overlord and Basilisk, skipping only Rapture for Void Helm plus off-meta Manta Scythe and Sky Splitter. Overlord's health-stacking passive and the armor shred from Basilisk are duelist tools, and Void Helm's 20% bonus healing received stacks directly onto Khaimera's own passive health regen from dealing damage. What the skipped Rapture would have added is on-hit bonus damage plus lifesteal, a sustained-damage tool for the extended jungle duels with Aurora and Legion that ran up the team's highest damage taken, 72,251, across five deaths. The healing amplification from Void Helm covers part of that gap but doesn't replace Rapture's extra damage output in a fight.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e.eternal: Demiurge multiplies whatever raw item stats are already on the build, a fit for a sustain-dueling jungler leaning on his own kit's health regen rather than a shield or cooldown tool. The trade is that all of Khaimera's durability has to come from the items themselves, since the loadout adds no flat health or armor of its own, which left less of a cushion in a matchup that read "theirs early" against Aurora's control kit.

fed26803-69a9-4fa1-b140-21f3cdf8d8e3.build: Matthewbernotas9's Akeron skipped all three winning-core items, Magnify, Tainted Scepter and Truesilver Bracelet, building Cybernetic Drive, Megacosm, Fire Blossom, Flux Matrix and Plasma Blade instead. Cybernetic Drive and Fire Blossom stack physical and magical armor with health, and Megacosm and Flux Matrix add percent-health damage and a magic-damage debuff, a heavily defensive path that explains the team's highest mitigated damage, 68,896. What it skipped was Tainted Scepter's 45% healing cut, the one item in his own recommended core built to answer Steel's sustain, on a team that carried only one anti-heal item all night. The defensive build kept Akeron alive, 3 deaths, the fewest on the team, but it left the healing-cut job to someone else who never picked it up either.
fed26803-69a9-4fa1-b140-21f3cdf8d8e3.eternal: Demiurge suits the same stat-stacking logic here: it amplifies whatever power, haste and penetration the items already provide, rewarding Akeron's item-heavy, damage-and-armor build without needing a specific rotation to make it work. Its trade-off is no built-in survivability beyond what the items themselves grant, which is less of a gap here since the actual build leaned so heavily on health and armor stats already, matching a bruiser trying to grind through Web Lash's root rather than burst and reset.

ed187ebf-450b-4f23-be5e-cb691e6328fe.build: Bman2295's Murdock completed the hero's exact winning core, Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator, then added Tainted Rounds and Onixian Quiver, the only anti-heal item anyone on the team carried. Lightning Hawk's stacking empowered shot and Imperator's bonus critical damage are the hero's core burst tools, and Tainted Rounds' healing cut plus scaling low-health damage were built specifically to answer Steel's sustain. The build gave Murdock everything the matchup called for on paper, but it still produced the team's worst kda and 9 deaths, seven of which were followed by a lost tower or objective within 90 seconds. The itemization matched the matchup; the fights it kept getting spent in cost the game.
ed187ebf-450b-4f23-be5e-cb691e6328fe.eternal: Demiurge fits a crit-and-attack-speed marksman core almost by default, multiplying the exact stats Lightning Hawk, Vanquisher and Imperator already stack rather than adding anything new. The trade is the same lack of built-in durability, which mattered on a low-mobility marksman whose kit gives him almost no escape once engaged, the same profile that shows up across his 9 deaths against Legion and Steel's dive pressure.

ae57df87-d868-498b-af8b-4562f987f67a.build: Muriel skipped all three winning-core items, Marshal, Crystal Tear and Windcaller, building Golem's Gift, Spellbreaker and Gaussian Greaves plus Timewarp instead. Crystal Tear and Windcaller both grant a 12% boost to outgoing healing and shielding, the exact stat that scales her shields for a pocketed carry, and none of her actual items carried that stat. Golem's Gift's armor stacking and Spellbreaker's one-time spell block are personal defensive tools instead, which didn't stop Legion from finding her in all seven of her deaths. Against a comp whose win condition is keeping a carry alive through bigger shields, the amplification missing from the build is the more direct answer than the armor taken instead.
ae57df87-d868-498b-af8b-4562f987f67a.eternal: Vesh adds a damage-over-time tick worth 6% of an ability's damage, plus 0.5% more per minute, to every ability hit that lands on a hero, the engine's top-modeled Eternal for Muriel. It gives no additional health, armor or heal-and-shield amplification of its own, so all of the survivability upgrade the build needed after skipping Crystal Tear and Windcaller had to come from the items instead. In a matchup that read "theirs all game" against Steel's peel, an item swap toward the heal-and-shield core would have done more for her than any Eternal choice could.

threats: Heal-stacking: Steel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought none.
Enemy is 4/5 magical — one magic-resist item goes a long way.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Akeron Web Lash (root 1s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Muriel) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

ourKits.combo: Alacrity shield+AS → Consecrated Ground bubble → Reversal global save
ourKits.winCondition: keep the carry alive with global shields and enable their damage
ourKits.passive: abilities grant Sentinel to allies; on-hit bonus
ourKits.playAgainst: she has no damage threat — dive her carry through the shields or pick her first

ourKits.combo: Void Breach slow → Cosmic Rift → Black Hole on the grouped enemies
ourKits.winCondition: land Black Hole / Cosmic Rift on a clumped team for AoE burst
ourKits.passive: an ability-empowered basic tethers a target for bonus damage
ourKits.playWith: hard engage that clumps enemies into his Black Hole
ourKits.playAgainst: immobile with long cooldowns — dodge the skillshots and dive him once Black Hole is down

ourKits.combo: Web Lash root → Crushing Maw armor shred → Hellfire eye → Consume pull-channel
ourKits.winCondition: root with Web Lash and grind with Hunger-stacked haste
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst on his rooted target
ourKits.playAgainst: dodge Web Lash — without the root he has no lock-down; interrupt Consume

ourKits.combo: Ambush leap → Unleash AS → Cull stun, Invigorate to cleanse+heal
ourKits.winCondition: stick on one target, stun with Cull and out-sustain via Spirit Regen
ourKits.playWith: follow-up burst inside his Cull stun
ourKits.playAgainst: ANTI-HEAL is mandatory — it guts his whole kit; kite the leap and CC through Invigorate

ourKits.combo: Static Trap root → Buckshot → Hot Pursuit AS → Long Arm of the Law global snipe
ourKits.winCondition: trap for the root, then out-range with Shots Fired and finish with the global ult
ourKits.passive: every 5th basic is a long-range bonus shot
ourKits.playWith: frontline/peel to protect his low mobility
ourKits.playAgainst: almost no escape — engage past the trap and he dies

enemyKits.combo: Boreal Sweep slow → Hoarfrost root → Glacial Charge engage → Cryoseism stun ult
enemyKits.winCondition: chain frost CC (slow→root→stun) to lock the fight down
enemyKits.playWith: burst that converts her long CC chain into kills
enemyKits.playAgainst: she's a CC battery — cleanse/QSS the Cryoseism stun; spread to avoid the chain

enemyKits.combo: Bull Rush knockback → Force Shield wall → Shield Slam knockup+stun ult, Shield Bash %hp
enemyKits.winCondition: peel the carry with walls/knockups or engage with Shield Slam
enemyKits.playWith: a carry he can wall for and peel
enemyKits.playAgainst: his Force Shield blocks projectiles — reposition around it; bait Shield Slam

enemyKits.combo: Rushing Beat dashes → Line Tempo wolves → Circle Rhythm shield → All-Kill! wolfpack ult
enemyKits.winCondition: stack Track and unleash All-Kill! in a grouped fight
enemyKits.playAgainst: spread vs the wolfpack; she's squishy without her shield up
